l.i: Divites in primis tempore famis pauperi-bus consulant: ideo enim Deus ipsos opib.in-struxit,ut alijs quoq; manu porrigant,quod multis modis fieri potest. Si habeas colonos quorum laboribus vineæ et agri non respon-dent, ne importunè eos urgeas ad solutionem debitorum. Incolas ædium tuarum ne vexes, nec pretium augeas, cogitans eos vix maximis laboribus panem, vestes, ligna, vedū[?] alia sibi comparare. Alios debitores ne ultra modū urgeas, ut tibi satisfaciant, præsertim si multos liberos habeat, et nō suo vitio ad paupertatem sint redacti: Mercenarijs persolue debitam mercedē: plus illis dato quàm petāt, si videas eos esurire. Elargire tuas eleemosynas illis quos nostri rerū necessariarum penuria laborare. D.Pau.1,Tim.6.hortatur di-vites, ut sibi in cœlis thesaurum colligant, & in pauperes sint liberales & benefici. Deus tuas opes auget sua benedictione, si ad victum & cultum corporis necessaria pauperibus distribuas. Superioribus aliquot seculis multi idola ex pretiosa materia fecerunt, sacrificia eis obtulerunt, suspenderunt anathemata,

page.notes: Right margin note 1 reads "Diuitum of ficium." in the scan; the "of-ficium" ligature is uncertain, so I wrote "Divitum officium." The first note sits beside "pauperi", where the line ends and the word continues with "-bus" on the next line. "vedū": the word in the list "panem, vestes, ligna, ..." is hard to read; it may be "vnedum" with a missing n. Read as "vedū" with [?] in the text. The printed "Diuites" and "Diuitum" use v as a consonant in the scan's spelling; I normalised them to "Divites" and "Divitum" per the u/v rule. Right margin note 2 "liberals / ter distrib." is split across two lines; the break after "liberali" is uncertain, so I wrote "liberali-ter". "D.Pau.1,Tim.6." is printed with a comma after the 1; kept as printed. Page marks: the printed running head is "ET FAME CONCIO. III." and the page number 59 is printed at the top right. The bottom signature "H 3" is printed under the text, at the right.
